title: Chalai gold heist: From Tamil Nadu to Karnataka, four suspects nabbed in Kerala
content: Thiruvananthapuram: The police have nabbed four men in connection with the robbery of 2 kg of gold from a jewellery shop owner in Thiruvananthapuram's Chalai. They were apprehended in Wayanad. The stolen gold is estimated to be worth around 2 crore. Thiruvananthapuram City Police Commissioner told Onmanorama that the four men had initially fled with the gold to Tamil Nadu. The men then travelled from Bengaluru to Mysuru and then arrived at Muthanga in Wayanad. The police, who had been keeping a close watch, immediately nabbed the men in Wayanad. The duo who had stolen the bag from the jewellery owner had other criminal cases against them. The owner of the bike is also among the four men who have been held. Police are now probing into the background details of the other two involved. Only a small portion of the gold has been retrieved from the loot. Police are investigating the whereabouts of the remaining gold. The robbery took place around 10.35 pm on Thursday when Nandakumar, owner of Vaishnavi Jewellers in Chalai, was returning home after closing his shop. He was travelling on an electric scooter towards his residence at Manakkad when two men on a motorcycle intercepted him on Sabhapathy Road and snatched a bag containing the gold. Fort Police obtained CCTV footage from a nearby shop showing the suspects trailing Nandakumar before the pillion rider snatched the bag. The footage also showed the motorcycle speeding away towards Thakaraparambu via the Power House overbridge. Police launched an investigation based on CCTV visuals and other evidence, eventually tracing the suspects to Wayanad.
